text: Hello, I'm Didgee. This one's for you and your grown up. Snuggle up. Ready?
Before we start, let's do our big breath. Breathe in, and out.
Lovely.
Remember our last adventure? A picture on a screen shows only a little. Can you say it?
That's it. Screen me is a little slice.
Real me is the whole me. Today we take one more step.
Today we learn one big thing. Some things on screens are pretend.
Pretend means made up, like a story.
Say our special word. Pretend.
Look at these two dogs. One dog is a cartoon. He can talk, and drive a car, and fly to the moon.
The other dog is a real dog. He can bark, and run, and lick your face.
One of them is real, and one of them is pretend.
Pretend means someone made it up, like a story.
And guess what? Pretend is fun.
Cartoons, stories, superheroes, magic. We love pretend.
And here's a little secret about me.
I'm pretend too. I'm a cartoon. I'm not a real person.
But I always tell you the truth about it. That's our deal.
Real means it is really, truly happening.
And here's the tricky bit. On screens, some things are real, and some things are pretend.
Even a video with real people in it can be made up. Even grown ups have to stop and think.
Pause me here. And grown up, ask your little one:
Can you think of something on a screen that's pretend, and something that's real?
I'll wait.
When something on a screen makes you go, "Ooh, is that really true?"
That's the moment for our magic question. Is this real?
And here's the very best part. You don't have to know the answer all by yourself.
You have a helper. You have your grown up. Here's what that sounds like.
A child might say, "This video says if I don't share it, something bad will happen. Is that real?"
And the grown up says, "Ooh, good question. Let's think together."
"No. That one is made up. Nothing bad will happen. You were so clever to ask me."
See? Asking is the clever thing to do. Asking is being a detective.
Grown up, this one's yours. Pause me. Say it together:
When we are not sure, we ask. Then, a great big high five!
Now our magic question, three times. Big voices!
Is this real?
Is this real?
Is this real?
Tonight, play the real or pretend game. Watch a little something together. A cartoon, a video, anything.
Every so often, your grown up says, "Real or pretend?" And you point and shout your answer.
Real dog? Pretend dragon? Real rain? Pretend magic?
It's a giggly little game. And you're learning to be a screen detective.
Before I go, show your grown up one thing you remember from today. Anything at all.
Got it? Brilliant.
Remember, screens are better together. See you next time.
